key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence can non-destructively distinguish interfacial versus bulk degradation in perovskite solar cells, showing that PEABF4 initially improves ETL/perovskite passivation but later accelerates depth-spreading thermal degradation.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical diagnostic for tracking where recombination losses originate during aging, helping engineers optimize interfacial treatments and thermal stability in perovskite device stacks.
method: Use wavelength-dependent PL excitation to probe different depths in the perovskite film.
Compare PL decay behavior before and after PEABF4 treatment under thermal stress.
Interpret trends with diffusion-recombination simulations to separate surface recombination velocity from bulk lifetime changes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports PL signatures and simulation results showing that PEABF4 reduces interfacial recombination initially, but thermal aging broadens losses from the ETL/perovskite interface into the absorber.
watch_item: The approach is inference-based and depends on model assumptions in the diffusion-recombination analysis, so depth attribution should be validated against independent structural or spectroscopic measurements.
paper_title: Wavelength-Dependent Photoluminescence Mapping of Depth-Dependent Degradation Under Thermal Stress in Phenethylammonium Tetrafluoroborate Treated Perovskite Solar Cells
